longest_story.title: The Six Strangest Sleuths
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Commissioner James Gordon; Scortini; Victor Voice; Leo; Elmo Forbes (quick-change artist); unnamed India-rubber man; Jay Jandron (villain); Jandron's gang [Vern Shively; others unnamed] (villains)
longest_story.synopsis: When crooks rob the box office at a Vaudeville performers performance, Batman enlists the aid of six former vaudevillians to help track them down.
longest_story.notes: Script credit from Martin O'Hearn. Inker credit verified by Charles Paris.

longest_story.title: The House of Batman
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Commissioner James Gordon; Mayor of Gotham City; Mayne Mallock (villain); unnamed thief (villain)
longest_story.synopsis: A wealthy man leaves money to Gotham to build a downtown HQ for Batman, but the Caped Crusader is surprised when the city builds as House of Batman for him. But he is more surprised when he discovers that a noted thief is using this building as his HQ.
longest_story.notes: Inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: The League of Ex-Convicts
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Commissioner James Gordon; Ed Stinson (employment agency head); Mrs. Carruthers; Tom Blick (ex-con); Lucky Dennis (ex-con); Harry Weston (ex-con); Ralph Bellows (villain); Bellow's gang (villains)

longest_story.notes: Script credit from Martin O'Hearn. Inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: The Man Who Knew Batman's Secret!
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Alfred Pennyworth [also as Thaddeus Crane]; Commissioner James Gordon; unnamed President of Mammoth Movie Company; John Varden (villain); Varden's gang (villains)
longest_story.synopsis: Batman is seeking to capture John Varden, but the wily criminal eludes him. Meanwhile, an out-of-town detective named Crane enters the picture, accidentally discovering Batman's true identity, a fact well publicized by the media.
longest_story.notes: Script credit from Martin O'Hearn. Penciler credit verified by Sprang. Inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: The Challenge of Batwoman
longest_story.first_line: Keep moving, Batman!
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Batwoman [Kathy Kane]; Curt Briggs (villain); Brigg's gang (villains)
longest_story.synopsis: Batwoman believes that an amnesiac man she finds is really Batman and that she should re-train him in crime-fighting methods. Since Batman is injured and must stay out of action, he and Robin go along with her mistake, but the man is really the leader of a gang of crooks.
longest_story.notes:
Second appearance of Batwoman.

Script credit from Martin O'Hearn. Inker credit verified by Charles Paris. Letterer credit from Martin O'Hearn and Joe Desris.

longest_story.title: Batman's Secret Helper
longest_story.first_line: All these people assisted us in the past... but it's our unknown helper who's in danger!
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Fred Varrel (brother of Jim); James Wilkins (blacksmith); Bill Seton (a diver); Dr. Walter Thorne; Jim Varrel (villain, escaped con); Varrel's gang (villains, in flashback)
longest_story.synopsis: Criminal Jim Varrel watches a TV show on which Batman appears to personally thank ordinary citizens who have helped him put crooks behind bars, hoping to discover the identity of the person who betrayed him.
longest_story.notes: Penciler credit verified by Sprang.

longest_story.title: The Boy Who Adopted Batman
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Mr. Ryan (Policeman); Danny Benson; Mrs. Benson (Danny's mother); Slim Miller (villain); Miller's gang (villains)
longest_story.synopsis: Danny Benson, a boy without a father, often talked to the Batman statue in the park. One day, he tells the statue about a gang of crooks and eventually he assists in the round-up of the criminals.
longest_story.notes: Inker credit verified by Charles Paris.

longest_story.title: The Career of Batman Jones
longest_story.first_line: I can stop this mechanical clown easily, Batman--by hurling your batarang at its rear control-panel!

longest_story.synopsis: Having saved a young couple from a serious car accident, Batman is pleased to learn the couple have named their young son after him. But his problems begin when the young boy wants to also become a crime fighter.
longest_story.notes: Writer credit by Martin O'Hearn. Inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: Three Crimes Against Batman

longest_story.synopsis: Batman turns the table on a crook who has successfully stolen several of the Caped Crusader's prized trophies.
longest_story.notes: Inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: Crime-of-the-Month Club!
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Commissioner James Gordon; The Joker (villain); Blinky Dean (villain)
longest_story.synopsis: The attempted theft of a valuable flower ties in with a theory that the Batman has about the Joker being involved in a series of crimes, and discovers that the Crime Clown is selling plans for crimes to other criminals.
longest_story.notes: Script credit from Martin O'Hearn. Penciler credit verified by Sprang. Inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: The Gotham City Safari

longest_story.synopsis: Batman and Robin are invited to become members of the famed Safari Club is quickly followed by the murder of one of the members, and the Dynamic Duo soon find themselves on a "safari" to ferret out the killer...before he kills them!
longest_story.notes: Script credit by Martin O'Hearn; inker credit verified by Charles Paris.

longest_story.title: The Signalman of Crime
longest_story.first_line: In their time, Batman and Robin have fought and conquered...

longest_story.synopsis: A small time criminal moves to Gotham and initiates a series of crimes, dressed as the bizarre Signalman. But Batman solves the clues to Signalman's crimes and nabs him.
longest_story.notes: Script credit by Martin O'Hearn and inker credit verified by Charles Paris.

longest_story.title: Batman -- The Superman of Planet X!

longest_story.keywords: Bat-Cave; Bat-Jet; Bat-Plane; Bat-Radia; Batmobile; Gotham City; Planet X; Wayne Manor; Zur-En-Arrh

longest_story.title: The Secret of Mechanical City

longest_story.notes: Both art credits verified by Sprang.

longest_story.title: Batman in the Bottle

longest_story.notes: Inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: The City of Ancient Heroes

longest_story.title: Manhunt in Outer Space

longest_story.notes: Script credit by Martin O'Hearn and inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: The Battle of Police Island!

longest_story.title: The Arch-Rivals of Gotham City

longest_story.synopsis: The "Woman of the Year" contest has two finalists: Vicki and Batwoman, and the judges decide to give both ladies a chance to prove their abilities before they select a winner...a winner who gets a date with the Batman!

longest_story.title: The Failure of Bruce Wayne
longest_story.first_line: What's this?
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Alfred Pennyworth; Silas Wayne (Bruce's great-uncle); unnamed convict (villain); "Babyface" Muller (villain); Muller's gang [Arnie Briggs; rest unnamed] (villains)
longest_story.synopsis: Called to his dying Uncle's bedside, Silas, Bruce is told by him that he is disappointed that Bruce has not continued the family tradition of adventure. Bruce sets out to prove Silas wrong...and does in an unexpected way.

longest_story.title: The Ice Crimes of Mr. Zero
longest_story.first_line: A cunning mind had devised a fantastic method to utilize cold for...

longest_story.notes:
Script credit by Martin O'Hearn and inker credit verified by Paris.

Letterer credit by Craig Delich.

longest_story.title: Prisoners of the Sargasso Sea
longest_story.first_line: It was a sailor's myth come true...
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; prisoners of the Sargasso Sea [Flavius; Erik; Captain Jolly; Blackjack (villain)]; Blackjack's crew (villains)
longest_story.synopsis: While chasing a modern-day pirate, Blackjack, Batman and Robin are marooned in the Sargasso Sea. There they discover others who have been trapped for centuries by the seaweed and its strange age-defying gas, and with the help of these men they destroy Blackjack's weapons and escape in a repaired Batplane.
longest_story.notes: Writer credit from Martin O'Hearn. Inker credit verified by Charles Paris.

longest_story.title: The Secret of the Everglades
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Joe Osceola (Seminole Indian); tribal members; Ponce DeLeon (explorer, mention only); Mike Briggs (villain, trapper); Brigg's henchmen (villains)

longest_story.notes: Script credit by Martin O'Hearn. Inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: The Mystery Seeds from Space
longest_story.first_line: They fell from the sky without warning--

longest_story.synopsis: Tracking down the source of weird, sonic vibrations, the Caped Crusaders discover the existence of some alien seeds from space, all powered by an alien meteorite, the last of which is a formidable robot.
longest_story.notes: Inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: The Last Days of Batman

longest_story.synopsis: Carter Nichols sends the Dynamic Duo back to ancient Venice to gather evidence in a case, but only Batman returns, while Robin is shifted to Gotham City a few days into the future, where he discovers a new criminal will kill Batman.
longest_story.notes: Script credit by Martin O'Hearn. Inker credit verified by Charles Paris.

longest_story.title: The Mystery of the 49th Star

longest_story.synopsis: Batman is called to Alaska to recover 49 diamonds stolen from a rich tycoon.
longest_story.notes: Writer credit from Martin O'Hearn. Inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: Batman's Super-Partner
longest_story.first_line: Ha, ha!
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Alfred Pennyworth [The Eagle]; The Joker (villain); Joker's gang (villains)
longest_story.synopsis: Accidentally gaining super powers from a machine in the Bat-Cave, Alfred wants to use his powers to aid the Dynamic Duo as the Eagle, but he only hinders, not helps, them against the Joker.
longest_story.keywords: Bat-Cave; Gotham City; temporary super powers; Wayne Mansion

longest_story.title: The Million Dollar Puzzle

longest_story.synopsis: The Caped Crusaders are hot on the trail of some auction items that were stolen, each of which are clues to the location of $1,000,000!
longest_story.notes: Inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: The Web of the Spinner
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Batwoman [Kathy Kane]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; The Spinner (villain, introduction); "Peanuts" Gilson (villain)
longest_story.synopsis: While Batman and Robin are tracking a criminal called the Spinner, Batwoman is checking out a mystic, whom she believes is running a scam operation. The crime fighters paths cross when Batwoman checks out a lead to the Spinner that the mystic drops.

longest_story.title: The Hand from Nowhere
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Commissioner James Gordon; Lex Luthor (villain); Robin [Dick Grayson]; Bobby
longest_story.synopsis: Batman investigates reports of a mysterious giant hand and some aliens present at thefts of seemingly worthless minerals.
longest_story.notes: This story features the only time Lex Luthor appears in a Batman story by himself as the lead villain before the 1990's.

longest_story.title: The Second Batman and Robin Team
longest_story.first_line: Look!... Our son is in danger!

longest_story.synopsis: Alfred tests out his new typewriter by writing an imaginary tale of Robin growing to manhood and becoming the new Batman, adopting a new partner as Robin, and taking on a gang of crooks.
longest_story.notes:
Script credit by Martin O'Hearn. Penciler credit by Craig Delich; we previously credited Bob Kane.  

This is the first in a series of imaginary tales of Batman II and Robin II written by Alfred.  Next seen in the second story in Batman #135 (October 1960).
longest_story.keywords: Alfred's Tales of the Future; Imaginary Story

longest_story.synopsis: While trying to capture Big Jim Masters, Batman is subjected to an scientific experimental device that makes him unable to fight crime when he hears a siren or bell.
longest_story.notes: Writer credit from Martin O'Hearn at http://martinohearn.blogspot.com/.

longest_story.title: Batwoman's Publicity Agent
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Batwoman [Kathy Kane]; Bat-Mite; Bat-Hound [Ace]; group of un-named bandits (villains)
longest_story.synopsis: Batwoman and Bat-Mite team up to fight crime and the Dynamic Duo do not know what to make of it. The truth, that Bat-Mite is in love with the female crimefighter, is the reason that the imp from another dimension being in town.
longest_story.notes: Penciler credit by Craig Delich; we previously credited Bob Kane. Inker verified by Sheldon Moldoff.
longest_story.keywords: Ace Camera Company; Bat-Cave; Batmobile; Gotham Caller; Gotham City; Gotham City Gazette; Hi-Fi Exposition

longest_story.title: The Rainbow Creature

longest_story.synopsis: The Caped Crusaders, in South America to provide assistance to a leader, encounter a strange rainbow-colored creature that has emerged from a volcano.
longest_story.notes: Script credit by Martin O'Hearn and inker credit confirmed by Moldoff.

longest_story.title: The Return of the Second Batman and Robin Team

longest_story.synopsis: Batman's old foe, John Crandall, is released from jail and vows to destroy anything that is a monument to the Caped Crusader, and begins by capturing the new Batman and Robin team.
longest_story.notes:
Penciler credit by Craig Delich; we previously credited Bob Kane. Inker credit verified by Moldoff.

This is the second in a series of imaginary tales of Batman II and Robin II written by Alfred.  Last seen in the third story in Batman #131 (April 1960), next in the third story in Batman #145 (February 1962).
longest_story.keywords: Alfred's Tales of the Future; Gotham City; Imaginary Story

longest_story.title: The Challenge of the Joker
longest_story.first_line: Of all the criminals Batman and Robin have faced, none is more...

longest_story.synopsis: Batman faces the Joker, who, this time, uses the four basic elements to commit his crimes.
longest_story.notes: Script credit by Martin O'Hearn. Inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.synopsis: Robin informs Batman that he is quitting the team to join up with a new crime fighter on the scene, Mr. Marvel, although Batman doesn't suspect the real reason why.
longest_story.notes: Script credit by Martin O'Hearn and inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: The Secret of the Sea Beast

longest_story.synopsis: The Caped Crusaders investigate reports of a mysterious sea beast that has attacked ships and caused the disappearance of two passengers.
longest_story.notes: Script credit by Martin O'Hearn. Inker credit confirmed by Charles Paris.

longest_story.synopsis: Professor Milo builds an entire island covered with traps to kill Batman.
longest_story.notes: Script credit from Martin O'Hearn. Inker credit verified by Charles Paris.

longest_story.title: The Ghost of the Joker!
longest_story.first_line: The world thought he was dead...
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; The Joker (villain); two unnamed crooks (villains)
longest_story.synopsis: The Joker appears to die during a prison escape, but his ghostly figure survives to commit crimes and taunt Batman from beyond the grave.
longest_story.notes: Script credit by Martin O'Hearn at http://martinohearn.blogspot.com/. Inker credit verified by Paris. Letterer credit by Martin O'Hearn and Joe Desris.

longest_story.title: Batwoman's Junior Partner

longest_story.synopsis: The publicity that Bat-Girl gets after having captured a criminal called the Moth results in the humiliated criminal seeking his revenge on her.
longest_story.notes: Penciler credit verified by Sheldon Moldoff.

longest_story.title: Ruler of the Bewitched Valley
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Regan (detective); Hartley (villain, renegade scientist); Hartley's thugs (villains)
longest_story.synopsis: The Caped Crusaders follow a renegade scientist to Central America, where he has created a series of automated robots that fool the superstitious natives.
longest_story.notes: Script credit by Martin O'Hearn. Inker credit verified by Charles Paris.

longest_story.title: The Blind Batman
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; unnamed eye doctor; Dr. Pneumo (villain, bank robber); Pneumo's gang (villains)
longest_story.synopsis: A bump on the head renders Batman blind temporarily, so he creates a set of radar ear plugs that allows him to combat criminals.
longest_story.notes: Script credit by Martin O'Hearn from http://martinohearn.blogspot.com/. Inker credit verified by Moldoff.

longest_story.title: The Alien Feud on Earth
longest_story.first_line: They came from another planet -- and they were...

Script credit by Martin O'Hearn.

longest_story.notes: Script credit by Martin O'Hearn from http://martinohearn.blogspot.com/. Inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: Batman Becomes Bat-Baby
longest_story.first_line: Imagine Batman as a four-year old!

longest_story.title: The Boy Who Was Robin

longest_story.notes:
Script credit by Martin O'Hearn from http://martinohearn.blogspot.com/. Inker credit verified by Paris.

Story contains two separate giant prop sequences!

longest_story.title: The Invaders from the Past

longest_story.title: The Secret Behind the Stone Door
